findings.title: New middleware has no test; the old behaviour was only covered indirectly
findings.body: The code that adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname to the context moved out of `instrumentPluginRequest` into this new middleware. I found no test for `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, and nothing checks the middleware order in `CreateMiddlewares` (it must run before `LoggerMiddleware` for the log line to carry these fields). A small test would cover this. It would run each of the four instrumented endpoints and assert that `log.FromContext`-style attributes are present in the `ctx` the next client receives. A test that moves it behind `LoggerMiddleware` and fails would guard the ordering.

findings.title: Test name still refers to the old InstrumentationMiddleware
findings.body: The constructor was renamed to `newMetricsMiddleware`, but the test function is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. Rename it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` to match.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so calls made through it are not recorded
findings.body: `FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a different instance. Any code that logs via `logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, such as `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest`, will not show up in the `InfoLogs` of the logger the test holds. A test that asserts on the fake would see nothing. Returning `f` (as `logtest.Fake.FromContext` effectively does through `f.New()`) would let such assertions work.

contracts.action: Plugin request log line now gets plugin/endpoint/ds/user/traceID attributes from the context via logger.FromContext instead of explicit params
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: logRequest appended pluginId, endpoint, uname, traceID, dsName and dsUID explicitly, using pluginCtx and tracing.TraceIDFromContext. The context attributes were separately set in the metrics middleware's instrumentPluginRequest.
contracts.before_after: After: ContextualLoggerMiddleware (pluginsintegration.go:160) runs before LoggerMiddleware (line 161) and sets log.WithContextualAttributes. ConcreteLogger.FromContext merges every registered provider: the context-params provider in log.go:55 and the tracing provider that emits traceID in tracing.go:91. The same fields therefore still reach the 'Plugin Request Completed' line, provided the tracing service has been provided so its provider is registered.
contracts.visible_effect: Same fields in the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line, though their position in the line may change.
contracts.failure_mode: If ProvideService for tracing was never called (some tests), traceID is not emitted. Real server startup does call it. The wrapper's fallback `d.New()` is effectively unreachable because ConcreteLogger.FromContext always returns *ConcreteLogger.

summary: This is a refactor: the contextual-logger setup moves from the metrics middleware into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and the logger middleware reads the plugin and trace fields back from the context. Middleware order is right (contextual logger before logger middleware), and the tracing and context-attribute providers cover every field the log line used to add explicitly. The only implementers of `plog.Logger` (the wrapper and `TestLogger`) were updated, so nothing is left unimplemented. Findings are minor: no test for the new middleware, a stale test name, and a fake `FromContext` that drops recorded calls.
